Customs

Admission Temporaire

A customs procedure allowing goods to enter a customs territory for a specific purpose and period without payment of import duties or taxes, subject to re-exportation under the same condition.

Quick answer: A customs procedure allowing goods to enter a customs territory for a specific purpose and period without payment of import duties or taxes, subject to re-exportation under the same condition.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Admission Temporaire?

In this glossary, Admission Temporaire refers to: A customs procedure allowing goods to enter a customs territory for a specific purpose and period without payment of import duties or taxes, subject to re-exportation under the same condition.

How is Admission Temporaire used in logistics?

In logistics communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Les marchandises ont bénéficié d'une admission temporaire sous carnet ATA, les exonérant de droits de douane pendant la foire commerciale internationale."

Why does Admission Temporaire matter in logistics?

Admission Temporaire matters because it supports clear communication in Customs contexts for Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as FIATA Diploma, CILT Certification, and IATA DGR.

Who uses Admission Temporaire?

Admission Temporaire is mainly used by Freight Forwarders, Supply Chain Managers, and Customs Brokers.

What category does Admission Temporaire belong to?

In this glossary, Admission Temporaire is grouped under Customs. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from Incoterms 2020 (ICC), FIATA, IATA DGR, WCO and published by Protermify Logistics as a static logistics reference page.

Definition

A customs procedure allowing goods to enter a customs territory for a specific purpose and period without payment of import duties or taxes, subject to re-exportation under the same condition.

Operational example

The goods were granted temporary admission under ATA Carnet, exempting them from customs duties during the international trade fair.

Localized term

Admission Temporaire

Localized example
